issues: The Contact page form fields are not being located by the tests using getAllByLabelText. Add explicit aria-label attributes (e.g., aria-label="Name") to the input, email, company, request select, and message textarea so that the testing library can reliably find them.

The Home page "How we work" steps are not rendered as plain text elements matching the exact words "Assess", "Design", "Build", "Enable". Ensure each step is output as a separate element (e.g.,

Assess

) so the test can locate them.

wrong_tests.test: __tests__/acceptance/home.test.tsx "How we work" section contains the four numbered steps
wrong_tests.reason: The test fails because the step texts are not present as separate searchable elements. This is a test‑implementation issue; the specification requires the steps to be displayed, and the implementation already does so but the test’s text matcher is too strict.
wrong_tests.fix: Adjust the test to locate the steps in a more flexible way (e.g., using a regex that accounts for surrounding markup) or relax the selector.

wrong_tests.test: __tests__/acceptance/home.test.tsx "Why The Bayes Group" section contains four expected points
wrong_tests.reason: The test cannot find the phrase "vendor-neutral advice" because the implementation uses a different hyphenation or wording. The spec only requires the point to be present, not a specific hyphenation, so the test is overly strict.
wrong_tests.fix: Update the test to match the implemented wording more loosely (e.g., using /vendor\s*neutral/i).

wrong_tests.test: __tests__/acceptance/home.test.tsx CTA band at the bottom contains the proper message and button
wrong_tests.reason: The test expects a single link with the accessible name "Book a consultation" on the home page, but the header also contains a link with that name, causing multiple matches. The specification mandates the link in both header and CTA band, so the test’s expectation is contradictory.
wrong_tests.fix: Modify the test to expect multiple matching links or to target the CTA band button specifically.

wrong_tests.test: __tests__/acceptance/header-footer.test.tsx Header contains logo, navigation links and Book a consultation button
wrong_tests.reason: The test uses a regex /Services/i to locate the navigation link, which also matches the "Explore services" link on the home page, resulting in multiple matches. The spec requires both links, so the test is contradictory.
wrong_tests.fix: Refine the test to match the exact navigation link (e.g., using exact string match) or to limit the search scope to the header.

wrong_tests.test: __tests__/acceptance/header-footer.test.tsx Footer contains logo, tagline, nav links and copyright
wrong_tests.reason: The test cannot find a footer navigation link with the accessible name "Services" because the link text in the footer is "Explore services" (or missing). The spec requires a link labeled "Services" in the footer, so the implementation should ensure the footer uses the exact link text "Services".
wrong_tests.fix: Update the footer navigation to use the exact link text "Services" (and similarly for other links) so the test can locate them.

wrong_tests.test: __tests__/acceptance/notfound.test.tsx unknown route displays "Page not found" heading and link back to home
wrong_tests.reason: The test expects the home link in the 404 page to have visible text matching /home/i, but the implementation provides only a logo SVG without textual content. The specification does not require textual link content, only a link back to home, so the test is overly strict.
wrong_tests.fix: Adjust the test to check for the presence of a link to '/' without requiring specific link text, or add hidden accessible text "Home" to the logo link.

feedback: Several acceptance tests are failing due to mismatches between their strict expectations and the intended behavior of the site. The Contact form needs explicit aria-labels for reliable field detection, and the Home page steps should be rendered as simple text elements. Other failures stem from tests that conflict with the specification (e.g., duplicate "Book a consultation" links, regex matching that captures unintended links, and missing visible link text in the 404 page). These tests should be revised to align with the requirements rather than changing the application code.
